findings.title: Simultaneous successful status and scheduler abort faults the channel without producing any completion
findings.requirement: Every accepted command/fault must leave a stable scheduler-visible completion diagnostic; abort/status priority must not strand the FIFO head.
findings.detail: With one legal active command, adapter_done=1, a matching successful status handshake (0x80), and scheduler_abort=1 on the same edge, status_fire_w sets status_seen_r but has code 00. The abort block latches faulted yet suppresses code 50 because it requires !status_fire_w. The normal completion condition sees the previous status_seen_r and does not publish success on that edge; from the next edge faulted suppresses normal completion forever. Independent XSIM observed faulted=1 and head_active=1 with no completion for eight subsequent cycles. Reset is the only recovery.
findings.required_action: Define and implement explicit simultaneous abort/status priority so exactly one held completion is generated and the faulted head remains recoverable; add good-status+abort and error-status+abort directed regressions.

findings.title: run_002 is not represented by the repository's frozen engine module index
findings.requirement: Independent promotion must be anchored to a parent-approved frozen source index and expected SHA-256.
findings.detail: The frozen engine_module_index SHA eae571... remains internally valid but pins the run_001 command queue SHA 95e09d.... run_002 instead supplies an implementer-created integration_source_index SHA 8b223d... that pins the new command queue SHA 8d821f.... All run_002 files and the implementation report match that new index, but it has no frozen/approved status and no parent-supplied expected hash in this assignment. Thus the audited revision is identifiable but not yet a frozen promotable module contract.
findings.required_action: After resolving DM2-VER-001, parent-freeze a new run_002 module index and rerun the identity gate against its expected SHA.

promotion.note: The prior timing blocker is fixed, but functional abort/status atomicity and frozen revision identity remain blocking.
